main_body: Flat snow ground patch: light snow with dithered grey-green patches, repeating every 16px across a 4x3 tile block. It is a terrain surface, not a standing object.
top_band: none: a flat ground texture with no standing body, so the column scan shows only alternating snow and dark patch runs (L 228/200 against 86-149).
evidence: This is a terrain ground tile, so the top-plus-front-face contract for standing objects does not apply. There is no object body, no receding side face and no elevation drawing to fail. It is valid as flat terrain.

style.evidence: Measured: 8 distinct colours and a median of 8 per tile. That is well below the grass reference (26 per tile, 80 colours) but level with the paving reference (7 per tile, 7 colours). Flat-fill coverage is 0%. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the darks lean green-grey rather than being a black line. The snow ramp runs from near-white #f6f9fd through #dce5f1 to #bccade, with a bluish shadow tone. The dark patches use #8a9b95, #677874 and #4b5b58 with dither speckle, which gives real grain and no sticker look. The weakness is the visibly repeated 16px motif and the small palette. It still matches the paving reference in richness and has no flat areas, so it is acceptable.
